channel.title: Security Brief
channel.description: Original analysis and ranked cybersecurity news with links to original sources

item.title: The edge is where attackers get in: this week's firewall, VPN and remote-access exploits
item.description: Five exploited flaws in firewalls, VPNs, remote-support software and file-sharing servers show one pattern. The systems that sit at the edge of your network, and that administrators manage remotely, are the weakest link. Here is what to check first.

item.title: October 2026 Patch Tuesday: what the Microsoft feed shows and what to do
item.description: The Microsoft feed lists few entries, and most of them are updates to October's release rather than new fixes. The one item that needs planning is a .NET remote code execution flaw that Microsoft has not fixed yet. Identity Web and WSL need version checks if you use them.

item.title: Weekly M365 & Entra Briefing: 13 to 19 October 2026
item.description: Exchange sign-in problems after October Windows Server updates, an identity-based incident at ConnectWise that affected Microsoft 365 tenants, and why device-code abuse is still worth a Conditional Access check.

item.title: Hackers Exploit Critical VMware, Cisco, and Apache Flaws as Espionage Attacks Emerge
item.description: The U.S. Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) on Friday added four flaws impacting Apache Roller, Cisco Expressway, SAP NetWeaver, and Broadcom VMware vCenter to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV), citing evidence of active exploitation. The vulnerabilities are listed below - CVE-2026-129448…

item.title: China's 'Armory Castle' Lays Siege to VMware vCenter Zero-Day
item.description: During the last wave of major VMware vCenter security updates, a China-nexus threat group likely already had its next zero-day up its sleeve.

item.title: Critical Perforce Puppet RCE Exploited in Attacks
item.description: Tracked as CVE-2026-115731, it allows a client that holds any CA-signed agent certificate to execute code on the server. The post Critical Perforce Puppet RCE Exploited in Attacks appeared first on SecurityWeek.

item.title: Recent UnrealIRCd Vulnerability Exploited in Attacks
item.description: Tracked as CVE-2026-114713, the high-severity flaw allows attackers to execute commands with server/IRCOp privileges. The post Recent UnrealIRCd Vulnerability Exploited in Attacks appeared first on SecurityWeek.

item.title: Siemens Industrial Automation Software Products
item.description: View CSAF Summary On October 21, 2026, the Node.js project released security updates addressing a critical vulnerability in the Brotli decoder bundled with Node.js, commonly referred to as "Node2Shell" (tracked as CVE-2026-111497). The vulnerability is an out-of-bounds write that could allow a remote attacker to cause…

item.title: Five warning signs of ransomware breach before encryption or data theft
item.description: Ransomware attacks often involve credential theft, lateral movement, and attempts to disable security controls long before encryption begins. Acronis examines five warning signs that can help defenders detect intrusions earlier, contain malicious activity, and protect critical systems and backups.

item.title: Everything Is a Web Application, Including Your Firewall
item.description: One of the early targets of PHP2Shell exploitation was the firewall. On October 28, Palo Alto Networks confirmed that attackers were exploiting the two PHP vulnerabilities, CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619, against PAN-OS management interfaces exposed to the internet. Both flaws let anyone execute code on the web…

item.title: CISA Adds Four Known Exploited Vulnerabilities to Catalog
item.description: CISA has added four new vulnerabilities to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) Catalog, based on evidence of active exploitation. CVE-2024-10441 Synology DiskStation Manager (DSM) Improper Encoding or Escaping of Output Vulnerability CVE-2026-40217 BerriAI LiteLLM Unprotected Alternate Channel Vulnerability…

item.title: What We Missed: Nvidia CEO Scandal Rocks AI Industry
item.description: In this video, Dark Reading editors discuss some of the news they didn't get a chance to cover, from Jensen Huang's resignation from Nvidia to Microsoft's recent cloud outage.

item.title: SBC Medical Group Data Breach Impacts Over 2 Million
item.description: Threat actors accessed databases containing customer information associated with clinics in Japan. The post SBC Medical Group Data Breach Impacts Over 2 Million appeared first on SecurityWeek.

item.title: Critical Apache Roller, Axis Vulnerabilities Exploited in Attacks
item.description: Attackers are targeting Confluence Data Center through an Axis flaw and Apache is warning of attacks against Roller. The post Critical Apache Roller, Axis Vulnerabilities Exploited in Attacks appeared first on SecurityWeek.

item.title: Apache warns of Roller RCE vulnerability exploited in attacks
item.description: Apache has released security updates to address a critical Roller flaw that threat actors are exploiting to gain code execution on vulnerable servers.

item.title: N-able Kills Legacy APIs, Patches 17 N-central Zero-Days
item.description: The patches target recently disclosed zero-days, as well as vulnerabilities already exploited in the wild. The post N-able Kills Legacy APIs, Patches 17 N-central Zero-Days appeared first on SecurityWeek.

item.title: Amazon: China-Linked Hackers’ AI Agents Exploited Medical Software Zero-Day
item.description: A threat actor used autonomous Cairn AI agents to discover and exploit a critical MONAI Label vulnerability. The post Amazon: China-Linked Hackers’ AI Agents Exploited Medical Software Zero-Day appeared first on SecurityWeek.

item.title: N-able says recent security breach led to major service outage
item.description: N-able says attackers who breached one of its servers have caused a major outage affecting Mail Assure and SpamExperts Hosted Cloud services worldwide.

item.title: F5 releases emergency patches for critical BIG-IP RCE flaws
item.description: US cybersecurity company F5 warned customers to patch five critical BIG-IP vulnerabilities that attackers can exploit to trigger denial-of-service (DoS) or gain remote code execution.

item.title: Java4Shell Exploitation Attempts Begin as Vendors Rush Out Advisories
item.description: GreyNoise, WatchTowr and Cloudflare report probing and exploit attempts, while Cisco, Elastic, Red Hat and Siemens detail impact. The post Java4Shell Exploitation Attempts Begin as Vendors Rush Out Advisories appeared first on SecurityWeek.

item.title: Java4Shell Flaw (CVE-2026-114938) Enables Pre-Auth RCE in Jira, Jenkins, Keycloak and More
item.description: A Java flaw called Java4Shell can let attackers without an account run their own code on Jira, Jenkins, Keycloak, and three other widely used applications, says Calif, the security research firm that disclosed it this week. The flaw is present in Java 17.0.6 and later, and the vulnerable code runs only on x86-64 Intel…

item.title: MSP ScreenConnect Servers Targeted in Month-Long Campaign
item.description: More than 40 servers received over 688,000 requests exploiting CVE-2026-84869 to execute guest-pushed files. The post MSP ScreenConnect Servers Targeted in Month-Long Campaign appeared first on SecurityWeek.

item.title: FBI warns ARTEX AI hacking tool is powering global cyberattacks
item.description: The FBI is warning that hackers are using an AI-powered penetration testing framework called ARTEX to automate cyberattacks against organizations worldwide, including a recent ConnectWise supply-chain breach that compromised Microsoft 365 customer environments.

item.title: GnuPG Warns Critical GPGME Flaw Could Expose App Data via Malicious OpenPGP Keys
item.description: A malicious OpenPGP key with an unusually long user ID can trigger a critical memory bug in GPGME, the standard library that programs use to work with GnuPG. The GnuPG project warned yesterday that the flaw could be used to steal data from affected applications and has released fixed versions. The bug, tracked as…

item.title: CTO of ‘RansomwareHelp’ Indicted for Wire Fraud
item.description: The chief technology officer and co-founder of ransomwarehelp.com, a six year old Florida business that claimed to use “advanced cryptographic tools” to restore data locked by ransomware, has been charged with wire fraud after an FBI sting operation found the company was simply paying the attackers for a decryption…

item.title: n0n extortion gang leaks data of JPMorgan Chase, Visa, and Mastercard customers
item.description: Data belonging to customers of three of the biggest companies in global finance has been leaked online, after hackers breached third-party service providers working for JPMorgan Chase, Visa, and Mastercard. Read more in my article on the Hot for Security blog.

item.title: Bell Canada says 'agentic' hacker stole enterprise customer data
item.description: Bell Canada has confirmed that an "agentic" threat actor breached its systems on November 17, 2026, and stole enterprise customer data, including information from a system used to order and provision telecommunications circuits.

item.title: In Security, Words Matter as Much as Tools, Maybe More
item.description: From talking cloud security to using AI, cyber leaders are finding that clear, disciplined communication is now a front-line defense capability across the enterprise.

item.title: Microsoft named a Leader in the 2026 Gartner® Magic Quadrant™ for SIEM
item.description: We’re honored that Microsoft has once again been recognized as a Leader in the 2026 Gartner® Magic Quadrant™ for Security Information and Event Management (SIEM). item.title: Vendor data breach exposes Chase, Visa, Mastercard customer info
item.description: J.P. Morgan Chase warned it suffered a data breach after a cyberattack at a third-party service provider exposed customers' personal information and marketing data.

item.title: Still tracking company passwords in spreadsheets? You’re flying blind.
item.description: Tracking company passwords in spreadsheets can leave IT administrators unaware of weak, reused, or compromised credentials stored and shared outside approved systems. NordPass explains how centralized password management can improve credential visibility, identify security risks, and simplify secure password sharing.

item.title: Dozens of credit unions hit by supplier breach that went unnoticed for six weeks
item.description: Ireland’s Data Protection Commission told Recorded Future News on Thursday it had received more than 40 breach notifications from credit unions that used the Belfast-based company as a data processor.

item.title: European Commission Confirms AI-Assisted Cyberattack Disrupted Services
item.description: The Commission took certain services offline to contain the incident, but it has no evidence of a data breach. The post European Commission Confirms AI-Assisted Cyberattack Disrupted Services appeared first on SecurityWeek.

item.title: SonicWall Warns Gen 6 Firewalls Won't Get Security Patches, Even for Critical Flaws
item.description: SonicWall has urged all customers still running Generation 6 firewalls to retire and replace them immediately and stop exposing the devices on the internet edge, citing security risks fueled by AI-assisted attacks.
